idiom_name: Ktor routing { get("/orders") { ... } } handler per page
implementation_notes: Ktor binds one handler lambda per path: routing { get("/orders") { call.respondText(...) } }, where ApplicationCall carries both request and response, so the lambda is the page controller; Route extension functions (fun Route.ordersPage()) keep one page area per file. The classic controller class is replaced by the route handler, and shared behaviour is installed as plugins or interceptors (install(Authentication), route-scoped plugins) rather than inherited. Spring Boot's @Controller/@GetMapping methods are the mainstream alternative when the stack is Spring rather than Ktor.
pitfalls: Route handlers are suspend functions on the event loop: a blocking JDBC or file call without withContext(Dispatchers.IO) stalls every other request.
call.respond must be called exactly once per request; responding twice, or returning without responding, fails at runtime rather than at compile time.
Path patterns are exact: '/orders' and '/orders/' are different routes unless IgnoreTrailingSlash is installed, so the page 404s intermittently from cached links.
